label: Canada: Health Canada (Post-NOC changes)
summary: Post-NOC quality, safety and efficacy changes: Level I supplement, Level II (notifiable change for biologics, supplement for safety labelling), Level III notice and Level IV record. Pharmaceuticals follow the 2019 Quality guidance; biologics the 2026 framework and quality guidance.

categories.label: Not available in Canada yet
categories.rule: This route is not available in Canada yet; classify the underlying change in its own entry.

categories.label: Level IV: record of change
categories.rule: Implement without prior review; keep the record under GMP and annotate the documents in the next Level I or II filing.

categories.label: Level III: notice of change (annual notification)
categories.rule: Implement without prior review, then file the Level III form: pharmaceuticals at implementation (recommended) or in the annual notification; biologics within 12 months. Data within 30 days if asked.

categories.label: Level III: immediate notification
categories.rule: Notify Health Canada from 21 days before to 14 days after implementing; data within 30 days if asked.

categories.label: Administrative submission
categories.rule: File an administrative submission (no scientific review) and implement when Health Canada has processed it.

categories.label: Level II: notifiable change (biologics)
categories.badge: Wait for a no objection letter
categories.rule: File a notifiable change; implement only after Health Canada issues a No Objection Letter. Review target 90 days.

categories.label: Level II: supplement (safety)
categories.rule: File a Level II supplement (safety) for risk-management labelling changes and implement once it is accepted.

categories.label: Level I: supplement (SNDS or SANDS)
categories.rule: File a supplement (SNDS, or SANDS for a generic) and implement only after the Notice of Compliance.

HC-A1.2:1.text: The drug substance is a discrete chemical entity.

HC-A1.2:2.text: There is no Level I change to the route of synthesis or to the specification.

HC-A1.2:3.text: Evidence of GMP compliance is available for the new site, and it is listed on the establishment licence where needed.

HC-A1.2:4.text: The impurity profile and physical properties are unchanged.

HC-A1.4:1.text: Same physical state, and the same polymorph and particle size where solubility matters.

HC-A1.4:2.text: Same route of synthesis; no new impurity above 0.10% and no higher levels.

HC-A1.4:3.text: Sterilisation of the drug substance is not affected.

HC-A1.4:4.text: The drug substance is a discrete chemical entity.

HC-A1.4:5.text: No Level I change to the specification.

HC-A1.5:1.text: No Level I change to the specification.

HC-A1.5:2.text: Sterilisation of the drug substance is not affected.

HC-A1.5:3.text: The drug substance is a discrete chemical entity.

HC-A1.23:1.text: The new site holds an establishment licence or is listed on one, with evidence of GMP compliance.

HC-A1.23:2.text: The manufacturing process and controls are the same, with equipment of the same class and operating principle.

HC-A1.23:3.text: The process is validated at the new site (or a validation protocol is in place).

HC-A1.23:4.text: No Level I change to the specification.

HC-A1.23:5.text: The product is not sterile, or the new site already makes similar sterile products.

HC-A1.24:1.text: Equipment of the same class and operating principle.

HC-A1.24:2.text: The process is validated at the new scale.

HC-A1.24:3.text: No Level I change to the specification.

HC-A1.24:4.text: For a modified-release product, dissolution profiles are comparable.

HC-A1.25:1.text: Same type of process and the same operating principle.

HC-A1.25:2.text: No change to the specification apart from tightening.

HC-A1.25:4.text: Release characteristics and sterility assurance are not affected.

HC-A1.16:1.text: Excipients stay qualitatively the same (except colours or flavours not used for taste-masking).

HC-A1.16:2.text: Quantitative changes stay within the Appendix 6 ranges.

HC-A1.16:3.text: Release rate and other performance characteristics are unaffected.

HC-A1.16:4.text: Excipients do not affect absorption or solubility.

HC-A1.18:1.text: Performance characteristics such as release rate are not affected.

HC-A1.18:2.text: Safety and efficacy are not affected (strength identification is kept).

HC-A1.20:1.text: No change to the qualitative and quantitative composition or to the mean mass.

HC-A1.20:3.text: It is not a scored tablet.

HC-A1.2c:1.text: A valid CEP covers the new source and its specification is met.

HC-A1.2c:2.text: No Level I change to the drug substance specification.

HC-A1.2c:3.text: The impurity profile and physical properties are unchanged.

HC-A1.33:2.text: The new system gives the same or better protection.

HC-A1.33:3.text: Functional packaging (dose delivery) is not affected.

HC-Q-bio.2a:1.text: The new facility is in an existing approved site or under the same QA/QC oversight.

HC-Q-bio.2a:2.text: Same process, equipment class and controls.

HC-Q-bio.2a:4.text: Comparability shown for the batches made.

HC-Q-bio.43:1.text: Same filling process, equipment class and controls.

HC-Q-bio.43:2.text: The new facility is under the same QA/QC oversight or already makes similar products.

HC-Q-bio.43:3.text: Process validation and media fills done.

multipleChanges.rule: Changes that are related may be filed together; a series of individually minor changes can together warrant a higher level (contact Health Canada). The filing takes the highest level.

L1.label: Review 1 performance standard: 180 days (quality only), 300 days (clinical), 120 days (labelling only)

NC.label: Notifiable change review target: 90 days, then a No Objection Letter

L3.label: Pharmaceuticals: file at implementation (recommended) or in the annual notification. Biologics: within 12 months of implementation

L3IN.label: Notify from 21 days before to 14 days after implementation

ADMIN.label: Processed without scientific review; no fixed timing modelled

Compliance and site information (establishment licences, GMP evidence)
